transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Lee. Um, well, I'm mainly here because things have been really difficult at work lately. I'm a hairstylist, and... my hands just feel like they’re moving through glue. 

It's like, even just doing the basic stuff, like sectioning someone's hair or mixing color, it takes me forever now. I just can't seem to get my body to move at its normal pace. And people at the salon have actually started noticing that I’m just a lot slower than I used to be, so... yeah, that's what brought me in.
Besides the slowness, have you noticed feeling unusually sad, down, or having lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Um, most days I just wake up with this... this heavy, flat sadness right in my chest. It's just always there. It makes me feel like there's really no point in trying to build the life I was planning for myself. I just don't see the point in any of it right now.
Have you noticed any tremor, muscle stiffness, or changes in your balance or walking along with this slowness?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My muscles don't feel stiff or anything, and I'm not shaking or losing my balance. It's really just the slowness... like I'm moving in slow motion, but everything else works fine, I guess.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal?

No, I haven't. I've never really felt like that. I usually need my normal amount of sleep, and I definitely haven't had any times where I felt super energetic or... elated, or anything like that. It's pretty much just been this heavy feeling.
Have you noticed any recent weight gain, feeling unusually cold, dry skin, or constipation?

No, I haven't noticed any of those things. Um, my weight is pretty much the same as always. I haven't been feeling unusually cold, and my skin isn't dry... and no issues with constipation either. Everything physical like that seems normal.
How long have you been feeling this way—both the sadness and the slowed movements—has it been going on for a couple of weeks, or longer, like several months?

It's been longer than a couple of months. It's actually been going on for about a year and eight months now. It all started right after my hours got cut at the salon. My savings just started draining away, and... well, that's when this whole feeling really began.
Over this past year and eight months, has there been any stretch of two months or longer where the sadness and slowness lifted and you felt back to your normal self?

No, not for two months. Looking back at it, I've spent most of this whole decline feeling depressed and just... weighed down. There have been some shorter stretches where the sadness wasn't quite as prominent, but it never lasted long enough for me to feel back to my normal self.
Over this time, have you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything you used to enjoy, to the point where you just don't feel like doing them at all?

Yeah, I have. I used to... well, I used to really like chatting with my clients, and I'd always help out the newer stylists at the salon. I used to go hiking with my friends a lot, too. But now I mostly just keep my head down and avoid people. I just don't have that spark in me anymore to want to do any of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite—either sleeping much more or less than usual, or a significant change in how much you're eating—during this time?

My appetite has definitely changed. I've been skipping meals without really meaning to... I just don't feel hungry. Sometimes I'll realize at night that all I've had all day was coffee and maybe a few bites of something small. I've noticed my clothes have gotten a lot looser, too, so I know I've lost weight. As for sleep, I'm just so tired all the time, but the eating thing is what I notice the most.
You mentioned not seeing the point in building the life you were planning—have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or not wanting to be alive?

I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I do get these thoughts sometimes. Like it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. Then nobody would have to deal with me anymore, and I wouldn't have to feel like this.

Before this current episode began about a year and eight months ago, had you ever had a similar period of depression and slowing down at some earlier point in your life, followed by a return to feeling normal?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone, but nothing like this. This is the first time I've ever felt this way for so long. Before all this started, I was just... normal, I guess. Doing my job and living my life. I've never had a period where I just stopped functioning like this before.

Right now, how much are these symptoms affecting your ability to keep working and manage your daily responsibilities—are you still managing, even with difficulty, or have you found yourself unable to keep up with work and basic day-to-day tasks?

It's... it's definitely affecting everything. I'm really struggling at work. I'm a hairstylist, and lately, I've just been making mistakes with basic salon routines that I used to do in my sleep. I work a lot slower now, too. I've had to cancel on clients that I used to handle with no problem. Because of all that, my manager and my clients... they've lost trust in me. 

Outside of work, it's bad too. I've pretty much pulled away from all my friends. I just don't have the energy to see them. I also used to go to the senior center to give volunteer haircuts, but I completely stopped showing up for that. I just can't keep up with any of it anymore.

opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a first-ever depressive episode lasting ~20 months (no prior episodes, ruling out recurrent depressive disorder F33), characterized by pervasive low mood, marked psychomotor retardation, anhedonia, significant appetite/weight loss, fatigue, passive suicidal ideation without plan, and severe functional impairment at work and socially. No manic/hypomanic history (ruling out bipolar disorder), no psychotic features (delusions/hallucinations denied), and hypothyroidism was screened for and ruled out via absence of cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, or weight gain, and no extrapyramidal signs (tremor, rigidity) suggesting Parkinsonism. The severity, number of symptoms, and degree of functional impairment meet criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms (F32.2).
